newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposition calls general strike for Monday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition calls general strike for Monday.

text.p: Zaire's radical opposition has called for a nationwide general strike on Monday to force Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo to stand down.

In a communique widely distributed in Kinshasa, Joseph Olenghankoy, the parliamentiary leader for opposition veteran Etienne Tshisekedi's followers, said the move was like a referendum to test the movement's support in the nation.

"Kengo is unable to win the war in the east. He is not willing to organise the long-awaited elections this year, he wants to stay in power as long as possible," Olenghankoy told Reuters by telephone on Sunday.
"It's a test of popularity. We want to make sure we are still popular. It's a kind of referendum for us," he said.

Rwandan-backed rebels have seized a portion of Zaire along the border with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda. Rebel chief Laurent Kabila has given Kinshasa until February 21 to begin talks. The rebels want to topple his arch foe, President Mobutu Sese Seko, in power since 1965.
The radical opposition has called for negotiations to enable elections to take place by July as planned. It has never accepted Kengo's appointment as prime minister.
Olenghankoy said an effective protest on Monday also would signify wide support for the opposition's boycott of new bank notes, which it terms inflationary.
The radical opposition called a similar protest in 1995. It flopped with businesses and government offices working normally.
